Do you have difficulty moving your eyes vertically (up and down)?

Do you have a history of seizures?

orders: Bedside examination of voluntary saccades and pursuit in all directions
Video-oculography (VOG) to quantify horizontal saccade velocity and amplitude
MRI of the brain with thin cuts through the pons and midbrain
results: 1. Bedside examination of voluntary saccades and pursuit in all directions
smooth pursuit and saccades: ocular motor apraxia - failure to initiate voluntary horizontal saccades with compensatory head thrusts
2. Video-oculography (VOG) to quantify horizontal saccade velocity and amplitude
video-oculography / eye-movement recording: failure to initiate voluntary horizontal saccades with compensatory head thrusts; ocular motor apraxia
3. MRI of the brain with thin cuts through the pons and midbrain
MRI brain with gadolinium: cerebellar vermis hypoplasia with molar tooth sign; no abnormal enhancement
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Joubert syndrome (caused by a mutation in genes involved in primary cilia function, such as C5orf42 or TMEM67)
Alternatives: COACH syndrome (Cerebellar vermis hypoplasia, Oligophrenia, Ataxia, Coloboma, Hepatic fibrosis)
Alternatives: Arima syndrome
